findings.headline: Rename readOnly to readonly.
findings.why: Solid 1 set the readonly attribute for readOnly. Solid 2.0.0-rc.23 declares only readonly in its JSX types, so readOnly is a type error, and it renders the name as written.
findings.guidance: Rename the attribute to readonly. The transform leaves this one because Solid 1 set readonly by truthiness, and Solid 2 keeps it for any value but false, null and undefined, so check the value too.

findings.headline: Rename tabIndex to tabindex.
findings.why: Solid 1 set the tabindex attribute for tabIndex. Solid 2.0.0-rc.23 declares only tabindex in its JSX types, so tabIndex is a type error, and it renders the name as written.
findings.guidance: Rename the attribute to tabindex. The transform leaves this one because Solid 1 printed a boolean value as text, and Solid 2 treats it as presence, so check the value too.

findings.headline: Rename className to class.
findings.why: Solid 1 set the class attribute for className. Solid 2.0.0-rc.23 declares only class in its JSX types, so className is a type error, and it renders the name as written, so class is no longer set.
findings.guidance: Rename the attribute to class. The transform leaves this one because the element already has class, so check the value too.

findings.headline: Rename htmlFor to for.
findings.why: Solid 1 set the for attribute for htmlFor. Solid 2.0.0-rc.23 declares only for in its JSX types, so htmlFor is a type error, and it renders the name as written, so for is no longer set.
findings.guidance: Rename the attribute to for and keep its value. The transform makes this edit.
